sentences: AI infrastructure startup Simplismart has raised $14 million in a Series B round led by Dallas Venture Capital, with participation from NVIDIA, Accel, Shastra VC and Micromax.
AI inference infrastructure startup Simplismart has raised $14 million in a Series B funding round led by Dallas Venture Capital , with participation from NVIDIA, Accel, Shastra VC and Micromax.
The funding will help the company strengthen its AI inference engine, expand its cloud provider network and grow across North America and other international markets.
According to media reports, the round values Simplismart at around $100 million post-money.
The startup had previously raised $7 million in a Series A round in October 2024.
Simplismart develops infrastructure that helps enterprises deploy and run AI models while optimizing inference costs, reducing latency and improving GPU utilization.
Its platform also enables cloud providers to turn their GPU capacity into AI services for enterprise customers.
The company said its annualized revenue run rate grew 14 times over the six months preceding the announcement.
Its customers include HeyGen, Higgsfield, InVideo, Shiprocket, Apna and Ema, which use its platform for production workloads across video, voice, multimodal and enterprise AI applications.
Simplismart also partners with cloud providers to deliver managed AI inference services.
At Yotta , its platform powers the serverless inference layer of Shakti Studio, allowing customers to run AI models without managing the underlying infrastructure.

Unlike providers that purchase or reserve GPU capacity and resell it, Simplismart focuses on the software layer that enables third-party GPU infrastructure to handle production AI workloads.
This approach allows cloud providers to offer AI services without building the entire inference stack themselves.
The company is also working with cloud providers and sovereign AI programs across India, North America, the Middle East, Australia and East Asia.

Simplismart plans to invest the new capital in its inference engine and orchestration platform while building partnerships to match AI workloads with available GPU capacity across regions and cloud environments.
